rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah account says Jacob recounts God's appearance at Luz, blessing, and promise of descendants and Canaan to Joseph.
rows.anchor: إن إله المواعيد اعتلن لي بلوز في أرض كنعان , فباركني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob dies and is buried with his ancestors in the purchased cave; Joseph grieves and arranges his father's burial.
rows.anchor: فمات ونقل إلى شعبه . فوقع يوسف عليه فقبله وبكى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's brothers fear retaliation, ask pardon in their father's name, and prostrate themselves; Joseph forgives them.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم : لا تخافوني لأني أخاف الله , أما أنتم فهممتم بي شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says God turned their evil into good by preserving many lives, then promises to provide for them and their households.
rows.anchor: فأحيي على يدي خلقا عظيما , والآن فلا خوف عليكم , أنا اقوتكم وحشمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before dying aged 110, Joseph says God will bring Israel to the promised land and asks that his bones be taken there.
rows.anchor: فأصعدوا عظامي معكم , فتوفي يوسف وهو ابن مائة وعشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the Torah account confirms the Qur'anic story and witnesses to its inimitability.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكر من القصة في التوراة مصدق لما في القرآن وشاهد بإعجازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the Torah omits that the brothers left after the cup episode, informed Jacob, then returned for provisions a third time.
rows.anchor: فمضوا إلى أبيهم فأخبروه بذلك , ثم عادوا مرة أخرى لميرة الثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī infers the omission was deliberate deception and says the written account fails rational scrutiny, confirming its authors' treachery and ignorance.
rows.anchor: فكأنهم أسقطوا ما في التوراة من ذلك تدليسا وتلبيسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Joseph account is revelation of the unseen; Muhammad was not present when Joseph's brothers agreed on their plot.
rows.anchor: أي النبأ العالي الرتبة الذي قصصناه قصا يعجز البلغاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since knowledge comes only by teaching and Muhammad witnessed none of this, God alone taught him; Biqāʿī calls this a conclusive theological argument against deniers.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنه لا معلم لك إلا الله كما علم إخوانك من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyān transmits from Ibn al-Anbārī that Quraysh and Jews asked the Prophet about Joseph.
rows.anchor: ولما سألت قريش واليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه السلام - كما نقله أبو حيان عن ابن الأنباري - عن قصة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet hoped the revelation would lead them to Islam, but they disappointed that hope; God consoles him that most people will not believe sincerely despite his desire.
rows.anchor: فأمل صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يكون ذلك سبب إسلامهم فخالفوا تأميله

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī defines the many as an amount exceeding another, and the greater portion as the larger share of a group.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : العدة الزائدة على مقدار غيرها , والأكثر : القسم الزائد على القسم الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no payment for the revelation, so his audience has no basis to accuse him of seeking their wealth.
rows.anchor: حتى يكون سؤالك سببا لأن يتهموك أو يقولوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder and an honor for all worlds.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الكتاب { إلا ذكر } أي تذكير وشرف

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī says dhikr is a meaning present to the soul; ʿālam ordinarily denotes a numerous group of knowable animals, with the cosmos named secondarily.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : والذكر : حضور المعنى للنفس , والعالم : جماعة الحيوان الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavenly signs include the sun, moon, stars, and clouds; earthly signs include mountains, trees, and animals, among countless others.
rows.anchor: أي كالنيرين وسائر الكواكب والسحاب وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs are clear to ordinary sight, but people ignore their indication of God's oneness while pursuing their pleasures.
rows.anchor: يمرون عليها } مشاهدة بالحس ظاهرة غير خفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many acknowledge God as Creator and Provider but worship others; hypocrites outwardly profess faith while concealing disbelief, and People of the Book follow scholars into rejecting other revelation.
rows.anchor: كانوا يقرون بأن الله خالقهم ورازقهم ويعبدون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can refer to subtle association through created means, since few move from means to their Cause; the Prophet called such association more hidden than an ant's tread.
rows.anchor: والآية صالحة لإرادة الشرك الخفي الذي أشار إليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
rows.claim: As quoted by al-Rāzī in al-Lawāmiʿ, al-Tirmidhī says the condition combines doubt and association; doubt is constriction of the chest during calamities.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام محمد بن علي الترمذي : إنما هو شك وشرك فالشك ضيق الصدر عند النوائب

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads their association as arising in their attention to passing thoughts and movements.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي : إلا وهم مشركون : في ملاحظة الخواطر والحركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes and threatens those who ignore evidence: a covering punishment from God could overtake them as it overtook earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: أي شيء يغطيهم ويبرك عليهم ويحيط بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour could arrive suddenly while they are entirely unaware; the final clause reinforces the suddenness already conveyed by baghtatan.
rows.anchor: أي وهم عنها في غاية الغفلة بعدم توقعها أصلا

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī cites Yazīd ibn Miqsam al-Thaqafī's verse as evidence for sudden surprise.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : قال يزيد بن مقسم الثقفي : ولكنهم بانوا ولم أدر بغتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that they are unaware adds emphasis to suddenness, already contained in the meaning of baghtatan.
rows.anchor: إنه تأكيد , لأنه معنى البغتة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الزبيدي
rows.claim: Al-Zubaydī defines baghtatan as a sudden surprise.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو بكر الزبيدي في مختصر العين : البغتة : المفاجأة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz defines mufājaʾa as arriving at someone while they are off guard.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبدالله القزاز في ديوانه : فاجأت الرجل مفاجأة - إذا جئته على غفلة

rows.speaker: ترتيب المحكم
rows.claim: The lexicon defines fajʾ as an event attacking without warning and associates it with speed.
rows.anchor: وفي ترتيب المحكم : فجئه الأمر وفجأه وفاجأه مفاجأة : هجم عليه من غير أن يشعر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's path is calling people to God by the Qur'an and Prophetic practice; it is clear, accessible, broad, and grounded in proof rather than imitation.
rows.anchor: الدعوة إلى الله على ما دعا إليه كتاب الله وسننه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his followers invite on insight, knowledge that distinguishes truth from falsehood as if the meaning were seen with the eye.
rows.anchor: لأن البصيرة المعرفة التي يتميز بها الحق من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following means that a later person seeks to join the first in the same place or in the matter to which the first called.
rows.anchor: والاتباع : طلب الثاني اللحاق بالأول للموافقة في مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every call to God must be joined to declaring Him free of deficiency; this placement hints at the callers' humility and request for pardon for shortcomings.
rows.anchor: منبها على أن شرط كل دعوة إليه سبحانه اقترانها بتنزيهه عن كل شائبة نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying he is not one of the polytheists is stronger than simply denying association: insight shows God has perfect attributes and no defect.
rows.anchor: أي في عداد من يشرك به شيئا بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī says the root of subḥān carries the basic meaning of disavowal from something.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : وأصله البراءة من الشيء

rows.speaker: ابن مكتوم
rows.claim: Ibn Maktūm glosses subḥān Allāh as declaring God free of consort, child, and evil.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مكتوم في الجمع بين العباب والمحكم : سبحان الله معناه تنزيها لله من الصحابة والولد

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh transmits Abū al-Khaṭṭāb's view that subḥān Allāh means God's disavowal of evil, citing al-Aʿshā's verse.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه : زعم أبو الخطاب أن ( سبحان الله ) كقولك براءة الله من السوء

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā uses subḥān to mean disavowal of a boastful ʿAlqama.
rows.anchor: قول الأعشى : اقول لما جاءني فخره سبحان من علقمه الفاخر أي براءة منه

rows.speaker: أمية
rows.claim: Umayya's poetic use of subḥānan with nunation shows that the word can appear as an indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: قال أمية : سبحانه ثم سبحانا يعود له وقبلنا سبح الجودي والجمد

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī calls subḥān a proper name for disavowal and purification, with definiteness and final n preventing declension.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جني : سبحان اسم علم لمعنى البراءة والتنزيه بمنزلة عثمان وحمران

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a Prophetic report explains subḥān Allāh as declaring God free of evil, a gloss also agreed upon by linguists.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : جاء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن قوله ( سبحان الله ) تبرئة لله من السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were human men like Muhammad, not angels or women; revelation came to them through angels, and they came from settled towns.
rows.anchor: أي مثل ما أ نك رجل , لا ملائكة ولا إناثا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for the view that earlier prophets were men, not angels or women.
rows.anchor: كما قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما , والرجل مأخوذ من المشي على الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Towns are settled gathering places suited to cultivating sound judgment, intellect, and knowledge; Mecca is the mother of towns.
rows.anchor: لأنها متهيئة للإقامة والاجتماع وانتياب أهل الفضائل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God sent no prophet from the desert, among jinn, or among women.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : وقال الحسن : لم يبعث الله نبيا من أهل البادية ولا من الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca combines town and desert virtues and gathers what was dispersed among earlier messengers, so its messenger is the final prophet.
rows.anchor: جمعت الأمرين وفازت بالأثرين , لأجل أن المرسل إليها جامع لكل ما تفرق في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī derives qarya and related words from a root centered on gathering and retention.
rows.anchor: بتراكيبها الخمسة عشر - تدور على الجمع , ويلزمه الإمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The q-r-y word family includes a town, resident, basin, collecting water, hosting a guest, and a communal vessel; Biqāʿī explains these senses through gathering.
rows.anchor: وقريت الماء في الحوض : جمعته , والمقراة : شبه حوض , وكل ما اجتمع فيه ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Related derivatives cover following a route, a valley where water gathers, a horse valley, and a shepherd's stick that gathers the flock.
rows.anchor: وقرى البلاد : تتبعها يخرج من أرض إلى أرض كاقتراها واستقرها - لجمعه بينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same root includes reading a page by gathering its knowledge, parts of a spear or sword, and a green bird associated with signs of rain.
rows.anchor: وقريت الصحيفة لغة في قرأتها - إذا تلوتها فجمعت علمها وكلامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī links qīr, the tar used to seal ship seams, to joining the ship's parts.
rows.anchor: وعلى كل تقدير هو ساد للشقوق والمسام فكان الجامع بين أجزاء السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī continues the q-r-y survey with terms for inquiry, incantation, ascent, and pure water, deriving them from gathering, joining, or retention.
rows.anchor: ورقيت الرجل بالفتح رقية : عوذته , ونفثت في عوذته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should travel to learn what happened to earlier deniers; destruction of wrongdoers and rescue of the obedient warns those who imitate their ancestors.
rows.anchor: والتذكير بأحوال الماضين من هلاك العاصين ونجاة الطائعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder to wait in Yūnus indicates God's anger at those who turn away from reflecting on His signs; sealed hearts do not benefit from signs.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما تقدم في سورة يونس من أن الآيات لا تغني عمن ختم على قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siyar is extended movement in a direction; naẓar is seeking apprehension by eye or heart, originally facing something with sight.
rows.anchor: والسير : المرور الممتد في جهة , ومنه أخذ السير , وأخذ السيور من الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better for the God-fearing than even an imagined thousand-year worldly life without pain and with abundance; reason alone should show this.
rows.anchor: وكان عيشها كله رغدا من غير آلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers endured prolonged rejection, mockery, and delayed punishment while warning their people; at last, when they despaired of victory, God's help came by defeating their enemies.
rows.anchor: وطال عليهم الأمر وتراخى النصر وهم يكذبونهم في تلك الإيعادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the light reading, the messengers' condition is rendered as despair while they answered mockers that the timing of God's promise was God's affair.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة التخفيف , وأما على قراءة التشديد فالتقدير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, as quoted by al-Zamakhsharī and al-Rāzī, explains the intensified reading as the messengers fearing their followers had called them liars after a long trial.
rows.anchor: نقل الزمخشري في الكشاف والرازي في اللوامع معناه عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha rejects the light reading because messengers would not suspect God of breaking His promise; she says the word is intensified.
rows.anchor: قالت : معاذ الله ! لم تكت الرسل تظن ذلك بربها

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha explains the light reading as the messengers fearing their followers had called them liars after tribulation and delayed help.
rows.anchor: قالت : هم أتباع الرسل الذين آمنوا بربهم وصدقوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saves whomever He wills; no one can repel His punishment from criminal peoples, however powerful, and prolonged testing trains followers in patience.
rows.anchor: أي عذابنا لما له من العظمة { عن القوم } أي وإن كانوا في غاية القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root k-dh-b centers on what lacks reality and extends to failed expectations, mistaken senses, and other false appearances.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( كذب ) تدور على ما لا حقيقة له , وأكثر تصارفها واضح في ذلك

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the phrase about three journeys as urging someone to undertake them, despite its surface declarative form.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأثير في النهاية عن الأخفش : الحج مرفوع ومعناه نصب

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī explains ʿAntara's kadhab al-ʿatīq as urging his listener to stick to the old wine, not denying it.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي في الحجة في قول عنترة : كذب العتيق وماء شن بارد

rows.speaker: محمد بن السري
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Sarrī reports a dialect difference: Muḍar uses kadhab al-ʿatīq with the accusative, while Yemen raises it.
rows.anchor: وحكى محمد بن السري رحمه الله عن بعض أهل اللغة في ( كذب العتيق ) أن مضر تنصب به وأن اليمن ترفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī prefers the simpler sense that truthful people remain protected, while lying makes one vulnerable; the idiom urges people to seize available opportunities for pilgrimage and jihad.
rows.anchor: وأقرب من ذلك جدا وأسهل تناولا وأخذا أن الإنسان لا يزال منيع الجناب مصون الحجاب ما كان لازما للصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom urges people to seize an opportunity before it becomes difficult; pilgrimage, minor pilgrimage, and jihad are available throughout the year under the conditions he describes.
rows.anchor: ولكون الكاذب يبادر إلى المعاذير ويحاول التخلص كان التعبير بهذا من باب الإغراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories from Noah to Joseph give sound minds lessons and show that God can honor Muhammad and grant him victory over every enemy as He did earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: يعبرون بها إلى ما يسعدهم بعلم أن من قدر على ما قص من أمر يوسف عليه السلام وغيره قادر على أن يعز محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is not fabricated as opponents say, but confirms earlier scripture and supplies details needed for religious, worldly, and afterlife matters, as well as guidance and mercy.
rows.anchor: { حديثا يفترى } كما قال المعاندون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī defines tafṣīl as dividing a whole by giving each part its due; the Qur'an guides and shows mercy to those who believe or can believe.
rows.anchor: والتفصيل : تفريق الجملة بإعطاء كل قسم حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing section follows the sequence of objections in Hūd: abandoning revelation, demands for a treasure or angel, and the charge that the Qur'an was invented.
rows.anchor: فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close of Joseph aligns with the opening of the next surah, affirming the revealed book as miraculous and true.
rows.anchor: مع اعتناق هذا الآخر لأول التي تليه , فسبحان من أنزله معجزا باهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surah, al-Raʿd, describes a true book whose effect varies: it can guide like thunder and rain, fail on barren land, or cause harm.
rows.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بأنه الحق في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Isrāʾ is a Meccan surah of 111 verses whose aim is exclusive turning to God, who owns all affairs and grants differing ranks; this is the path from tawḥīd to iḥsān.
rows.anchor: سورة الإسراء مكية - آياتها مائة وإحدى عشرالمقصود بها الإقبال على اله وحده , وخلع كل ما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names Subḥān and Banū Isrāʾīl express the surah's purpose through divine transcendence and the Israelites' history and journey to the holy land.
rows.anchor: وكل من أسمائها واضح الدلالة على ما ذكر أنه مقصودها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī and others report Ibn Masʿūd saying that al-Isrāʾ, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ṭā Hā, and al-Anbiyāʾ are among the earliest surahs and his treasured inheritance.
rows.anchor: بنو إسائيل والكهف ومريم وطه والأنبياء إنهن من العتاق الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Isrāʾ follows al-Naḥl's warning against haste and its promise of help to God's allies, confirming divine power through the extraordinary night journey and honoring Muhammad.
rows.anchor: افتتح هذه بتحقيق ما أشار الختم إليه بما خرقه من العادة في الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥān is an emphatic declaration of God's transcendence, governed by an omitted verb.
rows.anchor: وهو علم للتنزيه , دال على أبلغ ما يكون من معناه , منصوب بفعل متروك إظهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening word answers rejection of the night journey and signals its extraordinary greatness, which cannot be fully described.
rows.anchor: وهو راد لما علم من ردهم عليه وتكذيبهم له إذا حدثهم عن الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using asrā bi- rather than a transitive construction highlights the Prophet's accompaniment and honor.
rows.anchor: واختير القاصر للدلالة على المصاحبة زيادة في التشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase God's servant identifies Muhammad as the most honored servant, who served no one besides God or idols.
rows.anchor: أي الذي هو أشرف عباده وأحقهم بالإضافة إليه الذي لم يتعبد قط لسواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite laylan minimizes the time: the journey and ascent took only a small part of the night, without prior exercise, because the Prophet was already prepared.
rows.anchor: وليدل بتنوين التحقير على أن هذا الأمر الجليل كان في جزء يسير من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place the Prophet asleep at al-Ḥaṭīm, in the Hijr, or in Umm Hāniʾ's house; the last is the majority view, so mosque can mean the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان نائما في الحطيم , وقيل : في الحجر , وقيل : في بيت أم هانئ - وهو قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Masjid al-Aqṣā was then the most distant mosque from Mecca; the Prophet led all prophets, saw signs, and returned during a fraction of the night despite a month's journey by camel each way.
rows.anchor: فصلى بالأنياء كلهم : إبراهيم وموسى ومن سواهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God blessed Jerusalem's surroundings with water, trees, prophets, angels, worship, fruit, and provision; saying around it is more eloquent than inside it.
rows.anchor: بالمياه والأشجار وبأنه مقر الأنبياء ومهبط الملائكة وموطن العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an omits the ascent because its audience might not grasp its proofs; the night journey was established by signs they knew Muhammad had not previously seen.
rows.anchor: ولعله حذف ذكر المعراج من القرآن هنا لقصور فهومهم عن إدراك أدلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey let Muhammad see heavenly and earthly signs with eye and heart, as Abraham had been shown the kingdom of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: السماوية والأرضية كما أرينا أباه الخليل عليه السلام ملكوت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports that at Bayt al-Maqdis the Prophet chose milk over wine; Gabriel said milk was the natural disposition and wine would have led the community astray.
rows.anchor: أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم ليلة أسري به بإيلياء بقدحين من خمر ولبن

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jābir reports that when Quraysh disbelieved the journey, God displayed Jerusalem's temple to the Prophet in the Hijr so he could describe it.
rows.anchor: لما كذبتني قريش قمت في الحجر فجلى الله لي بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet described Quraysh's caravan, including a gray camel at its head; they later saw it arrive as he had said, yet still called it magic.
rows.anchor: يقدمها جمل أورق كما قال محمد , ثم لم يؤمنوا وقالوا : إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is exceptionally endowed with hearing and sight, and full benefit from signs comes through knowledge.
rows.anchor: وكان تمام الانتفاع بذلك إنما هو بالعلم , وكان سبحانه قد خص هذا النبي

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī's al-Lawāmiʿ distinguishes spiritual, intellectual, clairvoyant, prophetic, and messengerly vision, all gathered in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والبصر على أقسام : بصر الروح , وبصرالعقل الذي منه التوحيد

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Tirmidhī report from Thawbān that God folded the earth for the Prophet and showed him its east and west.
rows.anchor: عن ثوبان رضي الله عنه أنه صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم قال : ( إن الله تعالى زوى لي الأرض

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: The two Ṣaḥīḥ collections report from Anas that the Prophet could see behind him as in front; Biqāʿī says sight was not confined to the eyes, since God can create it anywhere.
rows.anchor: وكان يبصر من ورائه كما يبصر من أمامه - كما أخرجه الشيخان وغيرهما من حديث أنس

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Aḥmad reports that the Prophet located Jābir's lost camel on a dark night and led him to it.
rows.anchor: فقال لي : هذا جملك , اذهب فخذه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying the Prophet saw at night in darkness as he saw in daylight; similar reports are attributed to ʿĀʾisha.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم يرى بالليل في الظلمة كمل يرى بالنهار

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmits ʿĀʾisha's statement that the Prophet could see in darkness as in light.
rows.anchor: حكى بقي بن مخلد عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت , كان النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم يرى في الظلمة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says Moses saw a small creature on Mount Ṣafā in deep darkness from ten farsakhs; al-Haythamī included it in his additions to al-Ṭabarānī's collections.
rows.anchor: وأسند عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم أنه قال : لما تجلى الله

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ allows that Muhammad's exclusive ability to see in darkness may have been granted after the night journey.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون اختصاص نبينا صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم بذلك بعد الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī suggests the report about Moses' extraordinary sight may explain why Moses is mentioned immediately after the night-journey verse.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا من مناسبة تعقيب هذه الآية بذكر موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the prior command to emulate Abraham might seem to rank him above Muhammad; al-Isrāʾ instead opens with Muhammad's distinctive honors and rank as the best of Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: كان ظاهر ذلك تفضيل إبراهيم عليه السلام على محمد صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A report established from Anas says Muhammad led all the prophets, including Abraham and Moses, in prayer during the night journey.
rows.anchor: وسى وغيرهما من الأنبياء من غير استثناء , هذه رواية ثابت عن أنس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet praising God for making him a mercy and universal warner, revealing the Qur'an, granting his community precedence, expanding his chest, lifting his burden, and making him first and last; Abraham acknowledges his precedence.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي أرسلني رحمة للعالمين , وكافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا , وأنزل علي القرآن فيه تبيان كل شيء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a report through Rabīʿ ibn Anas at the Lote Tree, God calls Muhammad beloved and written in the Torah, makes him a universal messenger, and grants his community first and last place and testimony to his messengership.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه من طريق الربيع بن أنس وذكر سدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The same report says Muhammad is the first prophet created and last sent, and receives the seven oft-repeated verses, the endings of al-Baqara, and the role of opener and seal.
rows.anchor: وجعلتك أول النبيين خلقا وآخرهم بعثا , وأعطيتك سبعا من المثاني

rows.speaker: شريك
rows.claim: A report from Sharīk says the Prophet saw Moses in the seventh heaven.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث شريك أنه رأى موسى عليه السلام في السماء السابعة
